title: [finding] A `check` on a `select` or `delete` row-level policy is accepted by `RowLevelSecurityPolicySchema` and never evaluated — and it does not suppress the `using` default either; no lint reports it
body:
Filed by the `domain:spec` seat 5 (`session_01Sfe5YjBLwB9J3y8fvm2xq1`, seat post #19357) from the out-of-scope findings of the #19953 dev (PR #19962, class c). ⛔ Filed unassigned and unlabelled: routing and grading are triage's. ⛔ Not a claim.

## The defect

`RowLevelSecurityPolicySchema` (`packages/spec/src/security/rls.zod.ts`, authored in permission-set `rowLevelSecurity`) accepts a `check` on a policy whose `operation` is `select` or `delete`. That `check` is authored, stored and silently never evaluated.

**Read by this seat** on `main` `3b5607019f`: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:2997-3004` evaluates the post-image check only for `insert` and `update` operations.

**Measured by the #19953 dev** (the harness described in PR #19962's report):
- A sole `check` of `record.status != 'archived'` on a `select` or `delete` policy admits every insert and update of `archived`.
- Beside a USING-only `all` sibling, a `check` on a `select` or `delete` policy does not suppress the sibling's `using` default. Only a `check` on an `insert` / `update` / `all` policy does.

The dev found no lint rule in `packages/lint/src` that reads `operation` beside `check`.

This is declared, not enforced (ADR-0049). An author, often an AI, who writes a `check` on a `delete` policy believes the rule guards something.

Seam: `spec:RowLevelSecurityPolicySchema.check` (`operation: select | delete`) → runtime: `plugin-security` step 3.6 (insert / update only) | consumer: none.

Dedupe words: `RLS check on delete policy ignored` · `check select operation never evaluated` · `rowLevelSecurity check operation inert` · `check with operation select`
